remaining_risks: PDF/Word client-side downloads rely on browser-level file generation APIs (Blob, URL.createObjectURL, and react-pdf iframe/blob streams). Browser-specific download policies may apply.
Scope creep before target-user validation remains a risk.
Overbuilding into SaaS features too early remains a risk.
Automated safeguarding scan is heuristic and practitioners must independently review content for sensitive field details.
recommended_next_step: Conduct practitioner usability evaluation of the three intake routes (Batch Observation Builder, Structured Text Paste, Tabular CSV/TSV Import).
notion_page_update: Implemented v0.9 Phase 7 Bulk Intake & Structured Import Engine on branch feature/v0.9-field-sensemaking. Solved manual data-entry friction by introducing three deterministic, client-side intake routes: Route A (Batch Observation Builder with narrative reader, bullet/paragraph segmentation helper, compact review table with inline text editing, bulk theme and reliability controls, and atomic Draft evidence batch persistence), Route B (Multi-Source Structured Paste ingesting '---' delimited blocks with automated header parsing, conservative ethics defaults, narrative safety scan, scope mismatch reconciliation, and exact duplicate detection), and Route C (Tabular CSV/TSV Import featuring zero-dependency RFC 4180 parsing, delimiter auto-detection, smart column mapping suggester, and preview reconciliation). Enforced provenance integrity and triangulation invariance (multiple observations from 1 source count as 1 independent source). Added 20 new Vitest tests (146 total tests passing across 13 files), technical documentation in docs/v0.9_bulk_intake_guide.md, and complete 7-step browser acceptance audit via CDP in headless Chrome across 11 screenshots. ESLint and Next.js production build pass cleanly.
